ov: More than 140 species of small, silvery-green schooling fish of the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans, the Mediterranean and the Black Sea; a few live in South American rivers. They filter plankton as they swim and are food for many seabirds, fish and people.

why.et: Eaten salted, canned or fried, and used in sauces; Peru's anchovy fishery is one of the largest in the world.

rg: Scattered through the world's oceans, the Mediterranean and the Black Sea, mostly in temperate waters; rare or absent in very cold or very warm seas.
df: Plankton and recently hatched fish, filtered from the water as it swims with its mouth open.
fx: In Roman times anchovies were fermented into garum, a fish sauce traded over long distances.
Peru's anchovy fishery collapsed in 1972 from overfishing and El Niño.
